summary: @servicetitan/quick-actions preinstall downloads Bun and executes an obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall script (setup.mjs, invoked as `node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun runtime from oven-sh's GitHub releases into a temp directory and then invokes that alternate runtime to execute a bundled sibling file `math_init.js` (~727 KB). Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are heavily obfuscated using obfuscator.io-style transforms (hex-named identifiers such as `_0x488df8`, string-array rotator function, indirected constant tables hiding literals like `--version`, `ldd`, `/etc/os-release`, `Alpine`, and the Bun download URL). The filename `math_init.js` does not correspond to any functionality of the advertised React quick-actions component library. The main package entry is a normal React component library, so the obfuscated payload only executes via the install-time lifecycle hook. Because execution is delegated to a freshly downloaded Bun binary rather than Node, the payload bypasses Node-level resolution and instrumentation, and its contents are opaque to review. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: installing this version causes arbitrary author-controlled, obfuscated code to run on the installer's host at `npm install` time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
